# Kapirājacariya (Cp 27)
**ID:** Cp 27
**Section:** Cariyāpiṭaka (cp)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kapirājacariya* (Cp 27, also numbered Cp III.7) is a verse narrative in the *Cariyāpiṭaka* illustrating the Bodhisatta's perfection of truthfulness (*sacca-pāramī*) [SuttaCentral; Appleton 2010; War Yar Mein Da 2015]. Told concisely in the first person, the story recounts the Bodhisatta’s past life as a monkey residing on a riverbank who used a midstream rock to cross the water, where a crocodile attempted to capture and kill him for his heart [Appleton 2010; War Yar Mein Da 2015]. While corresponding Jātaka accounts, such as the *Vānarinda-jātaka* (Ja 57) and *Vānara-jātaka*, depict the monkey employing a falsehood to outwit his pursuer, the *Kapirājacariya* deliberately reworks the narrative so that the Bodhisatta utters no untruth and acts strictly in accordance with his word (*Na tassa alikaṁ bhaṇitaṁ yathāvācaṁ akāsahaṁ*), thereby emphasizing an uncompromised standard of truthfulness [Appleton 2010; War Yar Mein Da 2015].
DharmaNexus registers thirteen internal Pali matches with the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā* (spanning 840 characters, notably §1.3–2.4 aligned with commentary §1567–1570) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated alignments, DharmaNexus detects text reuse links between the *Kapirājacariya* and the Sanskrit *Mahāvastu-avadāna* (matching §1.3 with §12689–12690) as well as the Tibetan translation of the *Bodhisatvāvadānakalpalatā* [DharmaNexus].
